newsitem.title: USA: U.S. late spot propane follows crude higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. late spot propane follows crude higher.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices were steady to higher late Friday tracking stronger crude oil prices, players said, and helped somewhat by planned maintenance shutdowns of two Texas fractionators, traders said.

Mont Belvieu propane was offered at 35.0 cents a gallon, hanging on to a 0.75-cent gain seen at midday that traders attributed to short-covering and firmer May crude, which settled 49 cents higher at $19.91 cents a barrel.
"It was very active with crude coming up," one Houston player said, adding propane was also helped by petrochemical company buying.
Conway propane firmed a half cent for the day, with deals done at 35.00 and 35.12 cents a gallon, traders said, also helped by crude strength.

Sources said two adjacent fractionators in Mont Belvieu, Texas -- the 110,000 barrel-per-day Gulf Coast Fractionators unit operated by Conoco and the 105,000-bpd Mont Belvieu 1 unit run by Koch Oil -- were taken down for planned maintenance earlier this week.
"They are really brief turnarounds for three or four days. They're both coming back in a day or two," said one official familiar with the Mont Belvieu 1 operations.
